In summary, our research is concerned with
prosodic cues of discourse planning in Mandarin SpnNS and the comparison with RS.
the prosodic and paralinguistic features of spontaneous speech, and their applications to speech technology.
discourse prosody of SpnNS and the implications for speech recognition and synthesis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the acoustic cues in SpnNS reflect the planning process of the discourse structure, which is more complex than that of RS, while the acoustic cues in RS reflect the planning process at the lexical, syntactic and phonetic levels.
the prosodic properties of spontaneous narratives are more consistent with the properties of read speech than with those of casual conversation.
the prosodic properties of SpnNS are different from RS, and that the difference is consistent with the difference in discourse planning.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
discourse planning is reflected by prosodic patterns in the acoustic signals, and the patterns can be used to distinguish discourse boundaries in spontaneous speech.

the prosodic properties of SpnNS are more complex, but not less informative, than that of RS, and can be applied in automatic speech recognition, text-to-speech, speech synthesis, and prosodic analysis.
prosody is a powerful cue for discourse planning, but it is more so in SpnNS than in RS.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the acoustic cues in the speech signal are not only reflecting the linguistic content but also higher-level cognitive planning.
prosodic cues are more robust than lexical cues to identify discourse units, and that prosody should be considered a key factor in discourse planning.
prosodic patterns are more informative than the individual cues in the context of spontaneous speech.
